prompt:
Restore the PHOTOGRAPHIC QUALITY of this gardening book cover, using the original first image to recover detail lost by repeated generative edits. This is a repair, not a new design.
REFERENCE ROLES:
IMAGE 1 is the EARLIEST photographic artwork, BEFORE the damaging chain of later edits. Its vegetables are the authority for natural continuous photographic detail, fine leaf veins, coherent roots and stems, surface transitions and crisp object boundaries. Ignore its dark background, old title sprout and larger subtitle/sticker.
IMAGE 2 is ONLY the CURRENT LAYOUT AND COLOUR reference. It has the correct cream scrubbed-wood background, title without leaf icon, smaller subtitle, author, yellow ribbon and two stickers. Its vegetable surfaces are degraded: blurry swollen highlights, speckly stippling, dot mosaics, softened leaves and plastic colour patches. DO NOT copy those defects.
Reconstruct the original photographic vegetable groups from IMAGE 1 into EXACTLY their current footprints in IMAGE 2. Upper strip: tomatoes on vine at left, one red onion and half red onion near the centre, green pea pods at right. Lower strip: varied real carrots with fine feathery foliage at left and purple-stemmed curly kale at right. Preserve the original realistic irregular shapes and connected stems and the same overall arrangements. Carry forward the small tomato leaflet and pea tendril overlapping into the centre in IMAGE 2.
Restore true camera-like continuous colour, well-resolved leaf folds and veins, believable carrot root hairs and subtle natural skin marks. Remove the artificial dense DOTS, halftone-like speckles, pinprick noise, cloudy patches, swollen blocky highlights, chunky skin facets and mushy edges that accumulated in IMAGE 2. Avoid transferring excessive dotted droplets or soil peppering even from IMAGE 1: show predominantly clean tomato skins with only a few distinct natural droplets; carrots with sparse genuine soil traces and fine shallow root wrinkles. Photorealistic means subtle coherent texture, NOT noise or stippling. Keep natural leaf detail without waxy smoothing. No painterly, vector, cartoon, CGI, plastic or airbrushed rendering. No aggressive sharpening halos. Clean editorial food photography with soft diffuse daylight and clear but restrained highlights. Match the earlier source colours, with no artificial neon wash.
STRICTLY preserve the CURRENT cover design in IMAGE 2: same cream/ivory very pale scrubbed-wood surface continuously behind all sections, sparse low-contrast horizontal grain; same exact large rounded dark-green title "The Vegetable Guru" with NO leaf logo; same centred smaller two-line subtitle "Your at-a-glance" / "growing companion"; same "John Lennon"; exactly the same letter sizes, positions and line breaks. Same top-left narrow diagonal YELLOW ribbon with dark-green "100% Organic"; same small lower-left BLACK/GOLD circular "TRADITIONAL MEASUREMENTS" badge with weight symbol and unit lines "lb · oz" / "ft · in"; same tilted WHITE lower-right YouTube sticker with red play symbol and green "As seen on" / "YouTube" / "@Hackriculture". Keep both stickers the same size and positions, with crisp edges and lettering. No other changes.
Output ONE complete clean flat front cover, same 185:240 portrait proportion, at the highest native resolution available, preferably 2200 x 2860 or greater. Reconstruct detail from the EARLIEST photographic source, not by enlarging or oversharpening the damaged image. The result will be inspected as enlarged crops: faces of tomatoes, carrot skin and kale leaves must look genuinely photographic rather than a mosaic of dots. No labels, proof marks or mockup outside the cover.
